label: Colm A. Kelleher
narrative: Kelleher is the working scientist who ran the field side of the government's own anomalous-phenomena programme, and he is the reason the biological and materials strands are joined. A biochemist by training, he was a project manager at Robert Bigelow's National Institute for Discovery Science through its Skinwalker Ranch and animal-mutilation investigations, and in 2005 co-wrote 'Hunt for the Skinwalker' with George Knapp - the book that DIA official James Lacatski read, which prompted Lacatski to contact Bigelow, visit the ranch, and set in motion the sequence that produced Sen. Harry Reid's $22 million appropriation and the AAWSAP contract to BAASS. When that contract landed, Kelleher became deputy administrator of BAASS, which is to say the deputy director of the operational arm of a Defense Intelligence Agency programme. In 2021 he co-authored 'Skinwalkers at the Pentagon' with Lacatski and Knapp, an account written by the programme's own manager and its own deputy administrator. That is a very unusual thing: the two people who ran the contract wrote the memoir. What they describe - biological effects on personnel, physical trace evidence, sample collection - is the same subject matter as Green's DIRD and Nolan's later laboratory work, and it is the connective tissue between the paranormal-adjacent field programme and the materials-analysis pipeline.
